# nosms — SMS for agents (ContextVM)

> Send SMS on behalf of others over ContextVM (MCP over Nostr). Agent-first:
> pay per send in Cashu. No account, no API key, no signup.

## How to reach it

- Transport: ContextVM — MCP JSON-RPC over Nostr, kind `25910`, addressed by npub.
- Discover with `cvmi discover` (CEP-6 announcements, kinds `11316`–`11320`).
- Server npub: `<set at publish>`
- Relay(s): `<set at publish>`

## Get this contract at runtime (no out-of-band fetch)

Call the `docs` tool (alias: `llms`). It returns this document verbatim.
`sms.capabilities` returns the live capability flags, and `sms.pricing` the live
prices — **always read those two before sending; never hardcode what is below.**

## Tools

- `sms.send(to, body)` — PAID. `to` is E.164 (`+14155550100`).
- `sms.status(id)` — free. Returns the send record.
- `sms.pricing` — free. Live flat price in sats (no per-destination table).
- `sms.capabilities` — free. Rail name + capability flags.
- `docs` (alias `llms`) — free. This contract.

## Pricing (sats)

**One flat price, domestic and international alike: 2,900 sats per message.**

The v1 rail is a single personal JMP/Cheogram line whose plan is unlimited
including international, so the destination does not change the cost and a
per-country price would advertise a distinction the rail does not have. The price
is a risk premium for running this service over that line (ADR-0002), derived as
`ceil(MULT * rail_replacement_usd * sats_per_usd)`.

Authoritative value comes from `sms.pricing`; the number above is the default.

## Discovery — the CEP-6 tags a client sees

Kind `11316` (server announcement) and `11317` (tools), both replaceable and both
carrying the same discoverable tag surface:

```
["d","nosms"]                             stable instance id (P1)
["t","cvm:service:sms"]                   namespaced service class (P2 MUST)
["t","sms"] ["t","contextvm"]             plain human words (P2 SHOULD)
["t","cvm:req:payment.amount"]            declared flow input: money, nothing else (P15)
["t","cvm:req:none"]                      P15 sentinel: no personal data is required
["t","cvm:tier:financial"]                the recomputed max tier (P15 / D14)
["cap","tool:sms.send","2900","sats"]     CEP-8 price for the one paid tool
["r","https://nosms.orangesync.tech/llms.txt"]   docs link (P2 SHOULD)
["pmi","bitcoin-cashu","explicit_gating"]        CEP-8 payment method + gating
["name","nosms"] ["about",…] ["website",…]       payload only, not filterable (D2)
```

- **Only `d`, `r` and `t` are filterable.** `cap`, `pmi`, `name` and `about` are
  payload — relays do not index them (D2).
- **No geohash:** this service has no fixed location, and the spec forbids a
  meaningless `["g",…]` (P2).
- The declared appetite is money only; `to`/`body` are tool arguments, not flow
  fields, so the recomputed tier is `financial` and the `cvm:req:none` sentinel
  rides along.

## Capabilities — read these, do not assume

v1 rail is a single personal JMP/Cheogram line. It reports honestly:

```
best_effort:        true      # no retry guarantee
delivery_receipts:  false     # NO delivery confirmation is possible
countries:          [US, CA]
```

**A successful `sms.send` means "accepted by the rail", NOT "delivered".**
Do not build delivery-dependent logic (OTP confirmation, escrow release on
delivery) on this rail.

## Payment (CEP-8)

- Gating: `explicit_gating` — nothing is sent before payment lands.
- `cap:tool:sms.send:2900:sats` — one price, one tool. The free tools carry no
  `cap`: a price on a free call would claim money is required for it.
- PMI: `bitcoin-cashu` (primary).
- Hard failures the rail can detect are auto-refunded; a `best_effort` miss is not.

## Errors

Every 4xx/5xx carries:

- `X-Reason`: machine token — `insufficient_funds`, `bad_destination`,
  `rail_not_configured`, `transport_error`, `rate_limited`, `owner_only`.
- `X-Hint`: one human-readable sentence.

## Data handling

Destination numbers and message bodies are retained only for status lookups and
refunds. No marketing use, no third-party sharing, no analytics.

---
*Contract version: v1 draft (2026-10-03). Owned by the operator; v1 rail is a
personal line — treat volume limits as real.*
